summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, having studied under Julius Jolly (~1911–1913). He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve was an Indologist and historian who studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1926–1928). She served as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and was at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

Irfan Habib is a historian working in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (1947–1953), and New College (1954–1957), and spent his career as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1991).

Irina Anatolyevna Svetovidova was an Indology scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1950–1955). She worked as a researcher at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1957–1968) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1968).

Irving Babbitt was a philosopher who studied at Harvard, Williams College, the University of Paris, and École Pratique des Hautes Études. He taught Romance languages at Williams College (1893–1894) and was an Assistant Professor at Harvard University (1894–1912).

Isaac Schapera worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town, and the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski (~1925–1929), later holding posts at Chicago (~1948–1949), the LSE (~1950–1969), and Toronto (~1953–1954).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning a doctorate from the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society (~1812–1826) and was a Professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1836–1847).

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a Tibetologist who studied at ULB, LASSAAD, Tibet University, EPHE under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert, Harvard, and Qinghai Nationalities University. She was appointed Full Professor at Laval University in 2007.

Isabelle Onians is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002. She is attested as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library in 2007.

Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held positions at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and became a professor at Collège de France in 2025.

Isaiah Berlin was a scholar of philosophy and history. After studying at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932), he held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Cambridge and Newnham College under Kenneth J. Saunders and Caroline Rhys Davids, she served as Newnham's librarian, was on Cambridge's governing body, and served as Pali Text Society's Honorary Secretary (1942–1981).
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts as a professor at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College, attested in 1976.

Isao Nishitani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held a post at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and serves as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Sanskrit College. He taught at Fort William College (1841–1846, 1849), served at Sanskrit College (1846–1849), and became director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1851.

Isidor Isaac Scheftelowitz was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger, later holding posts at the University of Cologne (1919–1933) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1933–1934).

Ismael Quiles Sánchez was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who was educated at institutions including Colegio Máximo de San Ignacio. He was a visiting professor at Georgetown University (1950–1965) and served as Vice-Rector and Prorector at Universidad del Salvador.

Iso Kern is a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University. He held academic posts at KU Leuven (1962–1971), Heidelberg University (~1973–1979), Zurich, Fribourg, and the University of Bern, becoming Titularprofessor in 1985.
Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a professor at both Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.
